goals: Mechanistic: estimate the spatial distribution of recharge across the Naches relief and its soil/forcing controls
Critical-test: determine whether a single uniform recharge value (claimed 500 mm/yr) is defensible or an over-simplified basin average
Validation: constrain the recharge-relevant slow states (water table) against USGS wells and the Fan-2013 prior, since recharge itself is unmeasured in-domain
key_processes: soil-texture control on drainage vs runoff partitioning

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM with SSURGO soils and NLDAS forcing resolves per-column recharge; spatial sampling across elevation×soil tests whether recharge is uniform. PFLOTRAN not needed for a recharge-flux estimate.

answerable: Spatial variation of ELM-simulated recharge/drainage across elevation and soil (NLDAS forcing IS elevation-resolved in CONUS, so the elevation gradient is genuine)
Whether recharge is uniform vs strongly banded — directly refutes or qualifies the 'exactly 500 mm/yr everywhere' premise
Water-table plausibility check against USGS wells / Fan prior

not_answerable.aspect: Direct validation that recharge equals 500 mm/yr
not_answerable.why: No recharge measurements exist in-domain (observations_missing); ELM recharge cannot be pinned to a measured truth
not_answerable.needs: in-domain recharge observations (e.g. chloride mass balance, baseflow-separation, lysimeter estimates)

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified (elevation band × dominant soil), plus data-pinned validation columns
sampling_strategy.n_justification: 4 elevation bands capture the NLDAS precip/snow gradient that most plausibly makes recharge non-uniform; 3 soil classes capture drainage-vs-runoff partitioning. 4×3=12 spans the driver space with one column per (band,soil) cell — the smallest set that can show whether recharge differs across bands and thus test the 'uniform 500' claim.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Concentrate at the rain-snow transition and upland bands where snowmelt-driven infiltration and highest precip make recharge largest and most variable; anchor at least one valley-floor column where recharge is expected lowest, to bracket the spatial range.
sampling_strategy.replication: None within cells at this stage; the 4-band contrast is the primary signal. Add replication only if within-band soil variance proves large.

sampling_plan.reason: Lowest-precip, warmest band — expected recharge minimum; brackets the low end and tests whether 500 mm/yr is unrealistically high here.
Transitional precip/soil regime; resolves how recharge scales between valley and snow zone.
Snowmelt-driven infiltration peak and strongest recharge variability — the band most likely to exceed 500 mm/yr.
Highest precip/snowpack band; brackets the recharge maximum and shows the top of the spatial range.
Validation columns pinned to well locations for WTD checking; count set by data density (see validation_design), not fixed here.

validation_design.comparison: none — flagged gap; the '500 mm/yr' claim cannot be co-located-validated. Report simulated recharge distribution vs the claimed value as a plausibility comparison only.
validation_design.metric: spatial mean & spread vs claimed 500 mm/yr (descriptive, not validation)

validation_design.comparison: co-located at well points (indirect constraint on recharge realism); Fan prior used as warm-start carrier and cross-check
validation_design.n_validation_points: unknown — depends on USGS well density in HUC 17030002

experiment_summary.validation: co-located at USGS wells (count data-dependent; may reuse nearest exploratory columns)
experiment_summary.primary_treatment: NLDAS-2 forcing (elevation-resolved), native SSURGO soil, Fan-2013 WTD warm start + spin-up years

requires_capabilities.why: recharge is a slow state; cold-start default 8.8 m WT gives ~0 spurious recharge
storage must equilibrate before recharge is stable
no recharge data exist in Naches
requires_capabilities.blocks: direct validation of the 500 mm/yr claim

requires_capabilities.capability: USGS well ingest + WTD comparison tool
requires_capabilities.why: needed to co-locate and score ZWT against wells
soil-texture stratification depends on gridded soils

assumptions: Naches (HUC 17030002) lies within CONUS, so NLDAS-2 elevation-resolved forcing applies and the elevation gradient is physically represented.
The user's '500 mm/yr everywhere' is treated as a hypothesis to test, not a constraint to confirm; the design is built to potentially refute it.
USGS wells fall within or near the bbox at usable density; exact count unknown.
open_questions: What is the source/definition of the claimed 500 mm/yr (basin-average vs point)? A basin average could coexist with strong spatial variation.
How many USGS wells fall inside HUC 17030002, and over what depth range?
Is any independent recharge proxy (baseflow separation at a gage, chloride mass balance) obtainable to enable real recharge validation?
